question.value: What are the dynamical processes (outflow origin and infall) in Orion KL, probed with high-excitation CH3CN and CH3OH lines and 1.3 mm continuum?

evidence.quote: To examine the dynamical processes and especially to uncover the origin of the outflow in this region, observations with tracers of high excitation temperature and critical density are needed.

findings_qualitative.value: Gas consists of jet-propelled cores in the ridge and dense cores east and south, shaped like a wedge ring; outflow has multiple lobes not driven by YSOs

evidence.quote: The outflow has multiple lobes, which may originate from an explosive ejection and is not driven by young stellar objects.

claims.hypothesis: Is the Orion KL high-velocity outflow driven by a YSO?
claims.experiment: Mapped high-velocity CH3CN gas and compared with YSOs, IRAC bubbles and H2 jets
claims.result: Multiple lobes overlapping JPCs; Source I and MM1 outside or not the center; four IR bubbles around BN
claims.finding: Explosive origin centered on BN, age <=1300 yr

evidence.quote: More theoretical analysis and observation are needed to confirm our identification.

claims.hypothesis: Is there infall toward Source I and hot core?
claims.experiment: Line profile analysis (inverse P Cygni, blue profile) of CH3OH and CH3CN
claims.finding: Gravitational collapse supports accretion formation of high-mass stars

evidence.quote: These observations may support that high-mass stars form via accretion model, like their low-mass counterparts.
